result.label: bug
result.what_to_change: In parseAmount, the character class used to strip currency symbols (`/[\s€$£¥]/g`) does not include the rupee sign ₹ (or alphabetic currency prefixes like 'CHF' or apostrophe thousands separators like Swiss 1'200.00), so amounts like ₹1,250.00 fail the final numeric regex and return null. Extend the symbol-stripping/normalization logic to cover ₹ and other common symbols/separators (and consider stripping known alphabetic currency codes and apostrophes as thousands separators).
result.evidence: src/util/money.ts parseAmount does `raw.replace(/[\s€$£¥]/g, "")` then requires the remainder to match `/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/`; since ₹ isn't in that character class, '₹1,250.00' still contains ₹ after stripping and fails the regex, causing schema.ts to throw IngestError('errors.badAmount'), matching the exact error reported.

input.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

In parseAmount, the character class used to strip currency symbols (`/[\s€$£¥]/g`) does not include the rupee sign ₹ (or alphabetic currency prefixes like 'CHF' or apostrophe thousands separators like Swiss 1'200.00), so amounts like ₹1,250.00 fail the final numeric regex and return null. Extend the symbol-stripping/normalization logic to cover ₹ and other common symbols/separators (and consider stripping known alphabetic currency codes and apostrophes as thousands separators).
